steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Law reform is necessary because society changes and the law must adapt to address new situations, correct injustices and keep pace with technology and social values

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Law Commission is an independent body established by the Law Commissions Act 1965 with a duty to keep the law under review and recommend reform

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Law Commission produces reports with draft Bills; however, implementation depends on Parliament — only around 70% of Law Commission recommendations are eventually implemented, often with significant delay

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Parliamentary reform through Acts of Parliament is the primary method of law reform; Parliament can change any area of law and is not bound by previous legislation

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When discussing law reform, consider all three agents: Parliament, the judiciary and the Law Commission — evaluate the strengths and limitations of each Use specific examples of law reform to illustrate your points — e.g. the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, Online Safety Act 2023, or Montgomery on consent When evaluating the Law Commission, always note the implementation gap — recommendations are not automatically enacted For technology questions, show awareness of specific legislation: Computer Misuse Act 1990, Data Protection Act 2018, Online Safety Act 2023 Remember that law reform involves balancing competing interests: security vs privacy, innovation vs regulation, tradition vs modernisation
